report.verdict: A marketing manager with strong lifecycle results, but a headline and About that leave the best work out.
write_up: You’re a marketing manager running lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand. The recent job gives a recruiter a reason to reach out, but the headline and About lean on phrases that could describe almost any marketer.
The welcome-series line is the model to use: it names what you rebuilt and connects it to a first-purchase rate change. Your current job also gives a recruiter the subscriber count, team and budget.

Start by bringing the lifecycle work into your headline and About. Then give the Lumen Street job a little more detail. Together, those changes would let someone hiring a marketing manager see your work without having to piece it together.

cards.line: Marketing Manager | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.cannot_tell: “Storyteller,” “Growth Mindset” and “Lifelong Learner” could sit under anyone’s name. You run lifecycle email and SMS for 410,000 subscribers. Put that specialty beside your title.
cards.example: Marketing Manager | Lifecycle email and SMS | Klaviyo
cards.question: Which of your lifecycle work and tools do you want to lead with?

cards.line: Results-driven marketing professional with 8+ years of experience driving growth across multiple channels. Passionate about building brands people love and leading high-performing teams.
cards.cannot_tell: “Results-driven” leaves out the result. Your welcome series gives you a much more memorable opening, in your own voice.
cards.example: I run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand with 410,000 subscribers. I rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.question: Is the welcome series the work you most want to lead with?

cards.where: Fernhill Outdoor Co., Marketing Manager description
cards.line: Rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to copy the approach from. It tells a recruiter what you changed and what happened to the first-purchase rate.

cards.line: Supported client accounts and helped with reporting.
cards.cannot_tell: “Supported” and “helped” leave your part of the account work open. Name the clients or reports you worked on while keeping those ownership verbs.
cards.example: Supported client accounts for [types of clients] and helped with [what you reported] [how often].
cards.question: What kinds of client accounts did you support, and what did you help report on and how often?

cards.cannot_tell: Leadership tells a recruiter less about your marketing work than the lifecycle and SMS work in your current job. Use the three shown slots for the skills you want to be considered for.
cards.question: Which three skills would you want a recruiter to filter by?

fit.why: Your headline and current title name Marketing Manager, and your Fernhill work covers lifecycle campaigns, a team and a paid social budget.
fit.level: manager, your current title and management of two marketing specialists
fit.note: “Marketing Manager” is in your headline and current title. “Lifecycle email” and “SMS” are in your current job; “Klaviyo” is in your Senior Marketing Specialist description. Someone hiring for this work may also search for segmentation, marketing automation and A/B testing. None appears on your profile, so add the ones you do. Move lifecycle email and SMS into your headline.
